newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian miner may list in London, up product.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian miner may list in London, up product.

text.p: Indonesia's state-owned PT Aneka Tambang said on Thursday it may seek a listing in London later this year and is working with Australian, Canadian and South African firms to expand its gold and nickel production.
"We are working with several foreign firms to boost our gold and nickel production in the coming years," president director Darmoko Slamet told Reuters.
"We may also seek listing in London apart from Jakarta later this year, but the final decision depends on the government," the firm's finance director Ki Agus Umar Tochfa said.
Indonesian state-controlled Tambang Timah, the world's largest integrated tin miner, is already listed in London.
Aneka Tambang currently produces 65,000 ounces of gold per annum, all of it from its wholly-owned Pongkor gold mine in West Java, Umar said.
Tambang expected to boost Pongkor's production to 160,000 ounces of gold per annum in 1998. The mine has around 2.7 million ounces of gold reserves.
The firm expected its gold joint ventures to help boost its total gold production to more than 250,000 ounces of gold per annum in the year 2000, Umar said.
Tambang is currently working with Australia's Newcrest Mining Ltd to mine gold in Gosowong, Halmahera, in the Molluccas.
The Gosowong mine is expected to produce over 110,000 ounces of gold annually from 1998, Umar said.
Aneka Tambang will be entitled to receive around 20,000 ounces annually from the Gosowong venture, while the rest would go to Newcrest. The venture had a development cost of around $64 million.

Aneka Tambang is also working with Australian firms Aberfoyle Ltd and Giralia Resources NL to explore for gold in Nusa Tenggara and with Canadian Celtic Minerals Ltd to explore for gold in Kebasen, central Java.
The firm is also working with Aberfoyle to explore for gold in Pangkut, north Sumatra. Tambang officials declined to give further details on the exploration works.
The firm planned to start production of 16,000 ounces of gold annually later this year at its wholly-owned Cikidang gold mine in West Java.
The firm is also working with several foreign firms to boost its nickel production capacity, Umar said.

Tambang is currently working with Australian QNI Ltd and South Africa's Gencor Ltd to explore for nickel in Halmahera in the Moluccas and with Australia's Broken Hill Proprietary Company Ltd (BHP) to search for nickel in north Sulawesi and in Gag Island in the Moluccas.

The company said the joint venture with BHP in Gag Island was expected to produce 64,000 tonnes per annum of nickel and 2,000 tonnes per annum of cobalt by the year 2000. The development cost would be around $320 million.
Tambang currently produces 11,000 tonnes of nickel in ferronickel per annum and 700,000 tonnes per annum of high-grade ore from its Pomalaa mines in southeast Sulawesi.
The firm's nickel Gebe laterite mine in the Moluccas currently produces 1.1 million tonnes per annum of high-grade ore and 1.0 million tonnes per annum of low-grade ore.
The firm declined to reveal Tambang's stakes in the ventures or other details.
